cells.remarks: Issued from Murasīmā. Records the royal gift of the village Pasikalā situated in Pōtā-vishaya, to two brāhmaṇas named Kēdāra and Ayya, the sons of Bhaṭṭa Dāddi, belong- ing to Kausika-gōtra and the prōvara of Bhārgava, Chyavana and Āpnavāna, and Āpastamba-sūtra, and students of the Kāvya-śāstra, and hailed from Kōnāmayūra and were inhabitants of Lōśārings, for the merit of the divine being, and for that of his own mother, as well as himself. The charter was engraved by Mahā- sōna of Vallabhaghōsha and the ongraver was Mahā- sandhivigrahika Malladatta, the son of Dhīradatta. In charac- ters of about the 12th century. Published in J.P.A.S. B., Vol. I (1905), pp. 12 ff. See Bhandarkar’s List, No. 1553.

cells.remarks: Issued from Viniśītapura. Records the gift of land in the country, to a brāhmaṇa named Kīrttidēva, the son of Narasimha and the grandson of Harsha, who hailed from Madhura and was resident of Jalajaddā in Kēsala, and who belonged to Kasyapa-gōtra and the prōvara of Kaśyapa, Avatsara and Naidhru[va] and was a student of the Vēdānta (Vij[nā]nōmāya-madhyandina-śākhā). For the merit of his parents and himself. The charter was composed by a person (name not given) who was the son of Allavamā and known to Mahāsandhivigrahika Rāyaka Dhīradatta, in the presence of Ubohalavānivāga and was engraved by Vijanōsin Michchhu. The charter records the renewal of the portion referring to a Sōmavaṁśī king named Svabhāvatunga and probably to his conquest of Chēdi. Published in J.P.A.S. B., Vol. I (1905), pp. 14 ff. See J. A. S., Leton, Vol. XIX (1953), pp. 117 ff. and Plates. See Bhandarkar's List, No. 1565.

cells.remarks: Issued from Yayātinagara. Records the royal gift of a village named Dēluḍī in the Tūlātā-vishaya in the Kōsalā country to a brāhmaṇa named Bhaṭṭa śrī-Mahādēva, who hailed from Vādalī in Sevā and the grandson of Paramēśvara, who hailed from Kāsī in Sevā and the son of Svāmidēva, with the rights of Antaraṅgī in Lavadī-vishaya, belonging to Kauśika-gōtra and with the prōvaras of Dēvarāta, Audala and Viśvāmitra, and who belonged to Kāsī. The charter was written for the parents and himself. The charter was written by Mahāsandhivigrahika Kārttika Tathāgata known to Mahāsandhivigrahika Mānēka Dhīradatta and was engraved by Vinīni (Viț.). No. 1905, pp. 10 ff. Bhandarkar's List, No. 1388.

cells.remarks: Records a grant of lands to the shrines of god Kailāsanāthamūrti, goddess Abhirāmī and Chidambarēśvara at Tirukkadavūr by the members of the seventy-four sects of the Abhijāti-Pañchāḷattār for the upkeep of a matha, garden and flower-shrine (nandavana), agasālai, Pillaiyār shrine, etc. The management of the endowment was entrusted to one Ādiyapādapaṇḍāram, who was also required to perform mahāpūjā, pūjā and other services in the garden. Subscriptions were also stipulated among the members of the sects for the maintenance of the endowment.

cells.location: Kodinar, Kodinar Tahsil, Amreli District. Stone in the Baroda Museum.
cells.place: Impressions received from the Superin- tending Archaeologist, Western Circle, Baroda. Findspot: A second slab in the same place. in the same Mandir. Pillar in Rudra Mahal in the same place. †
cells.remarks: Contains a praśasti of Nānāka, a poet in the court of (the Vāghēlā) king Vīsadhavala and refers to the grant of a village named Bagasara by the king to the poet, who received in addition a mansion in Broach and a grant to live and to worship Sōmēśvara. In the introductory part, a genealogical account of the poet's family is given. Records the construction of a building called Sārasvata-krīḍā-kētana by Nānāka. This was composed by Kṛishṇa, the son of the author of Kumārapāla-charitra and engraved by Pālhaṇa. Cf. Bhandarkar's List, No. 577. Published in Ind. Ant., Vol. XI, pp. 98-103.

cells.place: Stop-well of Rājāmatī in the niche to the left of the steps. Do. (Acc. No. 4087).
cells.date: Vikrama 1535, Śrāvaṇa-vadi, Māgha, [su. 5], Thursday=1471 A.D., January 28.
cells.remarks: Records the construction of the step-well by Rājāmatī, the daughter of Bhairavadāsa who was the son of Uvāra, the son of Chhujjaio of Siraṅgagara. Gives the details of the lavish gifts and donations made by several Sultāns viz., Alauddin (Khalfjī) of Mālwā, Muzaffara Shāh of Gujarāt, Husain Shāh of Jaunpur, Barbak of Pānduä, Sultān (name not given) of Delhi (i.e. Delhi), Tughluq Shāh of… [name not given] and others, and of the gifts made by Sultān (name not given) of Vidara (i.e. Bidar) to Rājāmatī. Also mentions one of Rājāmatī's sons named Rānachandra who was a musician and a favourite of Sultāns Ghiyāsud-din and Muzaffar Shāh. The teacher of Rājāmatī and the musicians were Vu(Bu)rahāmata-su(suhukhu), Mīlā and others. The writer was Muni Guṇasundara.

cells.location: PŌRBAṆDAR TAHSIL Kāpāḍa
cells.place: Stone fixed in the southern wall of a Śiva temple on the bank of the Rēvatīkuṇḍa.
cells.remarks: Gives the genealogy of the minister Sāmantasiṁha. He is stated to have installed an image Sālaksha-Nārāyaṇa called Sāmantanātha. It also states to have built a big temple and Sāmantasiṁha is also stated to have built a big temple and installed it in an image of Pārśvanātha in front of the temple of Nēmi (i.e. Nēminātha) at the fort of the Rēvatīkuṇḍa. The record is partly damaged. It is connected with Rēvatī-kuṇḍa at Dvāravatī (i.e. Dvārakā) with a new flight of steps, for the welfare of his mother. He also records the damages of the temple of Mādhava and its repair with those of (Gūpāl)a, Kshētrapāla, Arkēśvara and Kēdārēśvara as well as Baladēva and Rēvatī besides constructing a well with arghaṭṭa. The composer of the praśasti was Sōmēśvara, son of Mādhava. Published in Ind. Ant., No. 568. Published in Poona Orientalist, Vol. II, pp. 227-31.

cells.location: KAIRA DISTRICT CAMBAY TAHSIL Tārāpur
cells.place: Slab fixed in a well near the village.
cells.date: Vikrama 1518, Āśvina śu. 6, Mṛigashira-nakshatra, 1461 A.D., 25 September, Friday.
cells.remarks: Slightly damaged. Records the construction of a well at Tārāpur or Tārāpura, a village in the region, measuring 40 cubits in extent, situated to the north of Stambhāpura and ruled over by the Sultan Mahmūd, son of Muhammad, son of Vāgha who was the son of Rūpadā, of Stambhā-jñāti, belonging to the city of Gandhara situated on the shore of the sea. The composer of the praśasti was the poet Jaina, son of Dhara, Vyāsa of Stambhāpura, Sūradhāra Khēta, son of Dēvadāsa, a resident of Stambhāpura, executed the work. Mentions also one Jīthā, son of Jantrī Thākurasīha and also Gapi, the former's brother.

cells.location: Bayana
cells.place: Stone in the compound of Ukhā Mandir.
cells.date: Vikrama 1012, Māgha su. 12, Monday=955 A.D., February 6.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records the construction of a temple of Vishnu by the queen Chittralēkhā and the endowment made by her of two villages named Gōgapura and Nāgapallī as well as certain fields in Haḍhapallī to the same deity. It is also stated that the temple was built by the sūtradhāra Mēdapāṭa of Śrīpatha and a similar sum in the mayūrapīṭhikā of Vasvāṭa for the deity. A further gift to the deity of one dramma from every house in the village (?) is also mentioned. It is also stated that the temple was written by the Karasika Śrīsakki. The engraver was the goldsmith Śrīpāla. Also records the gift of the village Aluvaviraka to the same deity on the occasion of a solar eclipse probably the same day. Cf. Bhandarkar's List, No. 71. Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. XXII, pp. 120 ff., and plate.

cells.location: Āhār
cells.place: Sāraṇeśvara temple.
cells.remarks: Records the commencement of the construction of a temple of Mahāvīra. Mentions the names of persons like Vāhaḍa and the consecration of the image of Hari made by Vāhaḍa on the second date. Also records the gift of a number of drammas in favour of Mahāvīra. Mentions the number of persons (names given) of a number of elephants, horses, etc. passing through the village for the worship of the deity. The record was written by the Kāyasthas Pāla and Pīllaka. At the end is given a list of names of the artisans, etc. etc. Published in A Collection of etc. Bhandarkar's List, No. 2395. Published in A Collection of Prubril and Sanskrit Inscriptions, pp. 67 ff.

cells.location: Dewal
cells.place: Stone slab.
cells.date: Vikrama 1040, Mār- gaśīrsha ba. 7, Thursday=982 A.D., October 20.
cells.remarks: Gives the genealogy of the ruler. Records the construction of two temples one to Śiva and another to Pārvatī by the ruler and his queen Lakshmī and the endowment to these temples of some lands situated in the Maṇḍala of Bhūhañja. Published in Dewal.—Stone slab. The composer was Nēhila, son of Śivaruha. The writer was Dēva, son of Dēva, and the engraver was Sōmanātha, son of Kāmadēva who belonged to Kanyakubja and who is described as Taṅkavijñānāśalin. Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. I, pp. 75 ff., and plate. (with a garden, a tank, a well, an assembly hall and a gate way. Published in Mathurā Inscriptions, pp. 134 ff., and plate.

cells.location: Jālōr †
cells.place: ‘Idgāh. Above the northern mihrāb
cells.remarks: Bilingual. States that Alf Khān, with the title (i.e. popular name) Fath Shāh, a resident of Khabar, who was a disciple (khalīfa) of Bābā Jām, died of plague at the city of Jām and was given date and that the deceased's disciple Jām'a Sānad Khān with the title (i.e. popular name) ‘Anwār’ all constructed the mosque. Also gives names of witnesses Rahmat Khān, Mr. Afzal Khān, Mīr Aslām Khān, Muhammad Bāx Khān, Mīr Asad Khān, Ahmad Khān, ‘Alī Khān, Qāsim Khān, Bahrām Khān, Dodyāl Khān and Sher Singh, who were the disciples of Fath Shāh. The mason was Salāwat Ahmad and Faqīr Muhammad Shamsu'd-Dīn Qādir was the scribe.

cells.remarks: Damaged.
